event.summary: Busy request timing does not establish an actionable wake defect
event.detail: Reviewed commit: ba7cc0264028eebb39647deb1d25b055e6886935. TLDR: considered whether a launch waiting for a busy host can remain pending beyond its stated 60-second waiting allowance. Details: api.rs:5716–5764 sends Resume outside WakeBudget::within, excludes elapsed time only on success, and includes busy-refusal elapsed time when the next budgeted fetch runs. environment/lifecycle.rs:27–34 uses try_host_provision_lock for immediate HostBusy rather than awaiting the holder; change_with_manager:54–81 reads the binding before dispatch. SPEC_impl.md, Tensorlake hosts, lines 7114–7125 says: "All its waiting, busy refusals included, shares one 60-second budget that only the accepted Resume request does not spend, so a slow resume is never cut off." A request in flight can be the accepted slow Resume, so enforcing the remaining wait as its deadline would violate the explicit latter guarantee. No shipped route that deliberately waits behind busy ownership was found; ordinary delivery latency or a stalled local binding read is bounded by the existing request timeout and is not evidence of a separate busy-wait regression. Suggested bucket: other if an actual avoidable overrun route is established. Could-be-highest: no; no security or loss-of-work consequence identified. Confidence: confirmed source-based non-report decision, not observed runtime behavior. proposed_drop: source refutation of queued busy waiting plus the explicit never-cut-off accepted Resume constraint above; possible_cover: none. Original suspected consequence remains a possible delayed refusal under transport delay, but no actionable implementation defect is established. No tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: Container leftover deletion stalls unrelated GUI requests
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: while deleting an interrupted container in Settings, the same Farhelm page makes unrelated host/session reads and actions wait for that container's remote cleanup. Closing Settings does not release the wait. A slow cleanup can therefore leave host/session displays stale and make unrelated operations time out with a misleading configuration-save error. Details: api/environments.rs:76–92 routes a row-backed leftover to DELETE /api/hosts/{host}, otherwise DELETE /api/container-orphans, but invokes send_save(request). api.rs:2259–2268 registers a process-wide CONFIGURATION_SAVES ticket synchronously and holds it until the request returns. api.rs:2461–2506 makes send/send_read snapshot and await every such ticket before dispatch, consuming their own timeout. api/save_order.rs:27–65 and 89–108 establish that the ticket blocks captured requests until drop and reports "Request timed out waiting for earlier configuration saves" on their deadlines. Ordinary fetch_hosts uses send_read at api.rs:4603–4605 and fetch_session uses send at 3611–3613. The shipping UI reaches this path from ContainersSettings' confirmed Delete, containers_settings.rs:157–181, on spawn_forever, so closing Settings cancels neither the delete nor its ticket. The row-backed request waits through hosts.rs:1477–1500's connection hold, shared-connection release and provider.destroy before finishing. The contract deliberately excludes exactly this: SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus, lines 334–340: "host mutations can wait on remote operations and must not hold every read behind them." This is a remote host mutation, not a configuration change later session reads depend on. Use the ordinary send path while retaining synchronous request construction and spawn_forever ownership; request lifetime and configuration ordering are separate. Suggested bucket: high, material UX degradation on a slow or stalled cleanup, affecting unrelated hosts in the same client. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Caveats: terminals, event-feed sockets and page-side JavaScript calls bypass this Rust funnel and keep running; other clients are unaffected. The cleanup's request timeout eventually drops the barrier. No established security or loss-of-work route, so not highest. Original lead l3 is resolved to this finding.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Synthesis verdict: duplicate of caller-supplied g037/f3 latest line 10 and g038/l1 latest line 11; revise my earlier candidate rather than retain its blanket refutation. Original consequence preserved and bounded: temporary wrong recovery surface/blocked terminal access; no permanent failure or destructive consequence established. Direct rechecks: session_ops.rs:79–80 accepts stale=true regardless of Interrupted; :91–107 allows retirement once pending is empty, and :215–225 clears restart_succeeded. list/view.rs:3416–3419 publishes successful completion, requests a refresh and releases the pending row operation without a listing fence. Its request_listing at :2473–2474 goes through reader::request_read, whose :644–660 single-flight path can leave the earlier read in progress. commit_listing at :1945–1953 applies normal ReadGate admission then :1985 retires success. ops.rs:182–187 rejects only generations older than the last applied result, not ones older than Restart. aggregate.rs:547 captures host state before awaited cached_slice at :578; row_of at :357 derives stale from that snapshot, so a captured outage response may arrive after reconnection and successful Restart. A mounted SessionView retains independent current (:605); selection following updates title and requests detail (:1243–1262), not its status. If retirement happens before the deferred observer at :549–564, restart_revision still increments mount_generation, but erased success cannot set relaunched=true. terminal_absence (:3701–3707) then remains Interrupted for the old mounted nonstale current, keep_terminal_surface (:3714–3722) is false, and terminal_specs (:1709–1710) emits an empty set. A generation increment alone is not a terminal. Connected detail normally heals this; this finding does not claim that fresh connected detail serves cached Interrupted, nor that the numerical completion revision is lost. Supplied records independently source-check pinned Dioxus 0.7.10 task-before-effect scheduling; my direct checks confirm there is no source ordering/fence in these caller paths that requires observation or fresh detail before retirement. This is a conditional source interleaving, never observed execution. Contract: SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus :1134–1140 requires Restart completion reattachment and observation by a mounted view. Narrow surviving part of my old refutation: a NONSTALE Interrupted row fails read_confirms_run and cannot by itself retire this success. That fact does not apply to stale=true. Cross-batch boundary: g036/l1 latest line 7 at b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe uses a NEWER eligible listing above the old restart_listing_floor and can lose the then-existing terminal-kind override too. Restoring the floor addresses the pre-completion stale-evidence trigger here but not that eligible-listing/deferred-observer route; do not collapse their fixes solely because both can show the interrupted card. Suggested bucket: other, matching the established temporary surface consequence. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. event.summary: Interrupted restart says nothing remains although retirement can leave survivors
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: after an update failed to end every old-terminal process, Restart can kill surviving work although its consequence text says there is nothing left to stop. Details: status.rs:633–635 expands Interrupted's wording to include a Farhelm update while retaining "nothing left to stop". session_view.rs:199–201 asks only for Running, but an already-open Restart prompt renders current shown.status at 2595, so a question can remain through an update's Interrupted report; its answer derives stop consent from restart_prompt_stops_agent, false for Interrupted (status.rs:651–652). core.rs:12980–13013 still reaps the prior run's scope and descendants when there is no live pane. The retirement contract explicitly permits surviving processes while committing Interrupted and leaves a timed-out sweep for Restart/Delete, so the consequence sentence overstates the evidence. Could-be-highest: yes, surviving agent/process work can be terminated beyond the sentence that says none exists. Suggested bucket: highest pending independent assessment of the specification acceptance; no execution evidence, source-supported route only. Confidence: confirmed source and contract mismatch in the copy, with an explicitly accepted lifecycle omission. proposed_drop: the authoritative specification intentionally accepts the remaining cleanup on Restart. Exact text, SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server (recorded revision, paragraph beginning "Ending the old terminals"): "A sweep that runs out of time leaves the rest for the session's Restart or Delete: the conversion commits regardless." It also states: "A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)". These accept surviving-work cleanup/uncertainty; parent must independently judge whether they also cover this newly broadened consequence wording. possible_cover: none. Caveats: ordinary Interrupted clicks bypass the question; the consequence text is shown only when a Running question was already open and later renders Interrupted. The update itself was already intended to terminate old terminals, so whether the survivor is work the subsequent click must separately authorize is a material disposition question. No reproductions or runtime tests run. Lead l5 is resolved; retain as proposed_drop for the required independent check, not as an uninvestigated suspicion.

event.summary: Interrupted restart promises nothing remains before reaping surviving work
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: a Restart question left open while an update retires old terminals can tell the user there is nothing left to stop, then kill processes that survived the update. Synthesis verdict: retain the misleading-confirmation finding; withdraw the earlier proposed_drop inference. Acceptance of imperfect startup cleanup does not accept a later destructive answer describing a smaller consequence than it performs. Original potentially highest consequence preserved: surviving user-owned process work can be terminated beyond this displayed confirmation. Suggested bucket: highest. Confidence: confirmed source/contract conditional route, incidence unmeasured and no execution performed. Rendered authority: only Running initially opens the header question (session_view.rs:199–200, :2255–2264), but the open ConfirmSlot remains until an answer/Cancel/Escape; current status is not its opening key. A later render takes its same token at :2043 and draws restart_consequence(&shown.status) at :2594–2595. Interrupted now says "Interrupted by a host reboot or a Farhelm update — nothing left to stop; restart it:" (status.rs:634–635). This render derives restart_prompt_stops=false via :650–651 and session_view.rs:2008. Its captured answer consumes the rendered token at :2612 and calls confirm_restart(false) at :2621. It therefore authorizes restarting under the explicit assertion of no remaining process teardown. The button's generic tooltip at :2600 still says stop the running agent; that conflicts with, rather than repairs, the consequence sentence designated as the confirmation's substantive warning. Ordinary Interrupted clicks bypass a question; this misleading-confirmation route specifically requires a Running question already open, then the update/reconnected detail renders Interrupted before the answer. Cancellation/navigation which removes that view ends this route; it is not assumed to survive unmount. Actual teardown: startup conversion treats live old-kind rows as TerminalEnded (core.rs:7097–7114) with no terminal. OldTerminals::sweep runs recorded per-agent scopes, warns on failure rather than refusing conversion (old_terminals.rs:283–318), and its one startup deadline can expire with processes remaining. Restart probes entry.terminal; None becomes no live pane (core.rs:12845–12889). Both consent checks call refuse_unconsented_stop with alive=false (:12906, :12957), and that helper refuses only when alive && !stop_if_running && Running (:3784–3797). It does not guard surviving scope work. The no-pane path still calls reap_process_tree on ScopeUnits::recorded(entry.scope.clone()), outstanding roots and SweepTarget::AgentOnly (:12985–13010) before the new launch. Thus a startup sweep that ran out of its shared budget can leave an old agent/descendant for the later ordinary Restart sweep to kill despite false stop consent. This is shipped cleanup selection, not an inference from a stale display alone or a hypothetical second click. Exact acceptance preserved for independent adjudication: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, :2994–2995 says "A sweep that runs out of time leaves the rest for the session's Restart or Delete: the conversion commits regardless." At :2998–3000: "A failure anywhere is logged and never fatal (the maintainer chose to start anyway and treat old sessions as ended, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running)". Those statements expressly permit the leftover-work premise and later cleanup. They do not say a confirmation may claim there is nothing to stop while performing it. SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus, Answers bind to what was drawn (:1071 onward) says a confirmed handler acts on what the answered render showed, and source comments at session_view.rs:2000–2008 and status.rs:641–649 likewise say the rendered prompt bounds stop consent. Suggested correction: describe retained process cleanup honestly for update-interrupted sessions (or conservatively for Interrupted generally), preserving the accepted retirement behavior. proposed_drop: false; the exact previous proposed_drop basis remains quoted above and was reconsidered rather than erased. possible_cover: none. Caveats: the update itself intended to end these old terminals; that explains why startup cleanup is allowed but supplies no explicit acceptance of misleading later confirmation text. The sweep touches prior agent work, not terminal tabs. No persistent-file deletion or unrelated-process selection is asserted. No tests, builds, runtime observation or reproduction performed. All readily checkable routing, confirmation, guard and sweep premises were checked; actual incidence remains unmeasured.

event.summary: Check whether the old GUI interlocks block the supplied JSON-input route
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e, specifically its parent UI left mounted across the update. TLDR: caller-supplied g196/l1 describes literal pasted JSON being reinterpreted as grid terminal input, including control bytes, on a fresh unknown-kind old-page xterm surface; this may run unintended commands and lose work. This is supplied cross-group synthesis, not a new independent discovery. Source basis from the exact discovery-neighbours record: missing terminal kind defaults None, old mount selects xterm, missing stream notice chooses raw bytes, whole paste becomes one binary message and the updated input decoder can accept a valid GridInput Text. Required assigned-group check: whether note_build/App skew handling, terminal capability, frozen or modal isolation actually prevents that old surface from mounting or sending input before any paste. Suggested bucket if route survives: highest/security or loss of work. Could-be-highest: yes, literal document content can become unintended program input. Confidence: unresolved lead; own App/API interlock source checks pending. proposed_drop: false; original potentially applicable acceptance retained from g196: SPEC_impl.md Grid streams says "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working" and "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy"; these do not by themselves establish acceptance of successful instruction reinterpretation. possible_cover: supplied g196/l1 latest line10 owns this underlying concern. No payload construction, runtime test or reproduction performed. Next checks: old App build-skew render/withdrawal and API response admission plus terminal sync/backendCapability/inputFrozen paths. All original consequence and acceptance questions remain explicit.

event.summary: Old-page GUI interlocks do not block the supplied JSON paste reinterpretation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e; old loaded UI examined at its parent. TLDR: an old browser page can remain interactive through the grid-only update, mount xterm for a missing terminal kind and send literal pasted JSON as raw bytes that the new supervisor can decode as an input instruction. Original potentially highest consequence preserved from supplied g196/l1: document string escapes may become actual Enter/control input outside paste wrapping, running unintended commands and losing user work. Synthesis result: duplicate/supporting interface record for g196/l1 latest supplied line10, not an independent discovery. Required App/API interlock checks were completed and do not refute the fresh unknown-kind interactive-surface premise. Source: old api.rs:2522 calls skew::note_build for its side effect but returns successful resp unchanged at :2549; only authentication refusals have their separate error branch. old skew.rs:30–35 explicitly excludes blocking/render refusal/automatic reload; BuildSkewNotice at :287–293 is an ordinary PeerLine, not a modal. old lib.rs:2042–2098 uses skew only to show that notice and prioritize it over TokenPrompt, then retains the PreferencesGate/authenticated tree; it does not inert or unmount SessionView. old session_view.rs:1867–1881 maps mismatch to unattended reconnect/heartbeat policy, not an input veto. terminal.js:1593–1595 returns manual-only for revoked capability; :1632–1638 cancels in-flight recovery attempts, not all live islands; :3284–3301 refuses unavailable or unattended mounts while explicit opening/reclaim remain allowed; :3414–3436 deliberately permits reclaim and :3460–3465 manual reconnect. No backendCapability/inputFrozen global check exists in these parent paths. Source-established current-host ordinary path: missing agent_terminal decodes None in old lib.rs:520–521; agent_spec_kind preserves it at session_view.rs:3839–3849 and :1809 puts it in the mount spec; terminal.js:4650–4665 builds xterm for non-host, including null. spec.unavailable comes from session.stale, and the terminal DOM's inert mark is only shown.stale (session_view.rs:3167,3231), not skew; modal isolation applies only when an actual modal is present. A connected ordinary host with no modal therefore satisfies these gates. old terminal.js:4628–4634 installs paste through term.paste; :2232–2235 sanitizes pasted text but has no skew check; :4158–4159 sends raw encoded text whenever the socket is OPEN. Missing stream notice settles bytes at :5887–5915, while the updated helm no longer emits that notice. g196 source-checks whole-message paste dispatch, fresh xterm unbracketed default, unchanged browser-message relay and the new GridInput Text decoding/encoding; this record adds the assigned App/API/global-admission checks, without constructing a payload or independently reproducing that lower-layer result. Suggested bucket: highest/security or loss of work if retained. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: likely conditional route, not runtime observed; premise is the old page opening/reclaiming a connected unknown-kind terminal and pasting a small valid Text-shaped JSON document while the old surface remains unbracketed. Ordinary keystrokes usually detach instead, and an xterm surface whose program enabled bracketed paste can prevent this particular route. Exact proposed_drop basis preserved for independent review: SPEC_impl.md Grid streams :3022–3027 says "A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working" and "Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy". The full paragraph expressly discusses misdrawing and malformed-input attachment failure, not successful instruction reinterpretation; no drop or lowering is accepted here. possible_cover: supplied g196/l1 owns the same underlying defect; parent should treat l6 as duplicate/interface support. No additional readily checkable App/API/isolation premise remains; incidence and clipboard payload occurrence are unmeasured. No runtime test, payload construction, reproduction or live-install action. Lead l6 is resolved to this retained supporting finding before beginning the separate new search.

event.summary: Environment history keeps a decodable diagnostic host after deletion
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: checked whether reusable environment history becomes unreadable after its original disposable host is deleted because the new UI DTO still requires host: HostId. Pinned store/environment_history.rs:107–144 reads origin_host_id as HostId and decode_entry at :152–169 always emits that integer together with target: Some(...), canonical_cwd: None, cwd: ~ and creation_seq; sessions.rs:4468–4473 serializes those entries directly. The history intentionally retains the diagnostic old id without requiring the deleted host to exist. The new UI target field is defaulted for older replies and matches that serialization. Its caller draft.rs:1994–2021 bypasses installation-bound ordinary-history admission for target-bearing entries and selects the captured environment target, rather than reusing that diagnostic host as launch authority. Therefore deletion does not create a null-host decode mismatch or silently retarget a fresh launch. Suggested bucket if established: high for broken recent setups, but none established. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route; a wrong-host launch was considered but refuted by target-based admission. Confidence: confirmed source analysis. proposed_drop: source refutation above, not specification acceptance of harmful behavior. possible_cover: none.
